title: Little red dots as a cosmological probe: constraining $H_0$ with quasi-periodic pulsations
comment: 11 pages, 2 figures. PRL under review. Comments and suggestions are welcome
summary: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has uncovered a population of ``little red dots'' (LRDs) at $z \gtrsim 4$, potentially representing early supermassive black holes embedded in dense gaseous envelopes. The recent discovery of the lensed LRD RXJ2211-RX1 reveals significant variability on rest-frame timescales of decades, which may be interpreted as quasi-periodic variation that has a potential physical parallel to stellar pulsations. In this work, we derive an idealized, self-consistent period-luminosity-temperature ($P$-$L$-$T_{\rm eff}$) relation based on the hydrostatic envelope model. If this theoretical relation holds and can be empirically validated/calibrated, it would offer a novel framework for constraining the Hubble constant ($H_0$). The current sparse sampling of \tgta\ yields a preliminary $H_0 = 120.7_{-46.5}^{+47.0} \text{ km s}^{-1}\text{ Mpc}^{-1}$ as a proof-of-concept, with the error budget dominated by the uncertainty of the pulsation period. Our forecasting analysis shows that continuous monitoring over a 10-year baseline can reduce the $H_0$ uncertainty to 3-20\%, depending on the intrinsic pulsation period, while the systematic uncertainty floor remains to be fully characterized. This method offers a potential independent probe to measure luminosity distances in the early universe.

AI.tldr: The paper derives a period-luminosity-temperature relation for "little red dots" (LRDs) based on hydrostatic envelope models, applies it to the lensed LRD RXJ2211-RX1 to estimate H₀ = 120.7 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹ as a proof-of-concept, and forecasts that 10-year monitoring could reduce H₀ uncertainty to 3–20%.
AI.motivation: To develop a novel, independent method for measuring luminosity distances and constraining the Hubble constant using the quasi-periodic variability observed in little red dots (LRDs) at high redshift.
AI.method: An idealized, self-consistent period-luminosity-temperature (P-L-T_eff) relation is derived based on a hydrostatic envelope model for LRDs. The relation is applied to RXJ2211-RX1 to infer H₀, and forecast analysis is performed for monitoring strategies.
AI.result: A preliminary H₀ = 120.7_{-46.5}^{+47.0} km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹ is obtained. Continuous monitoring over 10 years could reduce uncertainty to 3–20% depending on the intrinsic pulsation period.
AI.conclusion: If empirically validated, the P-L-T_eff relation for LRDs could provide an independent probe of luminosity distances and H₀ in the early universe, with the systematic uncertainty floor still requiring characterization.

title: Strong environmental AGN enhancement among DSFGs in z > 2 protoclusters
comment: This manuscript has been submitted to A&A; the arXiv version reflects revisions made in response to referee comments
summary: Galaxy protoclusters (PCs) at z > 2 are dense regions in which cold gas availability and elevated galaxy interaction rates trigger intense, often dust-obscured, star formation. These mechanisms are also expected to promote super-massive black hole (SMBH) growth, but this effect remains unclear, largely due to heterogeneous galaxy selections and active galactic nuclei (AGN) identification methods in previous studies. We quantitatively assess the impact of PC environment on SMBH growth by measuring the incidence of X-ray AGN among dusty star-forming galaxies (DSFGs) in PCs and in a homogeneously selected control field sample, and investigate the physical mechanisms driving any difference. We consider ALMA-detected DSFGs in sub-mm/mm continuum of seven PCs at 2 < z < 4.5, and construct a selection-matched control sample from the COSMOS survey. We statistically compare X-ray AGN incidence and host galaxy physical properties obtained through uniform spectral energy distribution fitting. We find a significant enhancement of X-ray AGN fraction in PCs by ~2.7x (Poisson significance p = 3e-4). Similar values are found in two redshift bins: ~2.7x at z = 2-3 (p = 0.003) and ~2.6x at z = 3-4.5 (p = 0.03). PC and field DSFG samples are well matched in stellar mass, star-formation rate, and dust mass, ruling out selection effects or systematically higher host masses as the driver. Our results provide quantitative evidence that the dense PC environment enhances AGN incidence and SMBH growth in DSFGs beyond what host galaxy properties alone predict, likely through increased gas availability and interaction-driven fueling. This work is a first step toward a homogeneous assessment of environmental effects on SMBH growth across cosmic time.

AI.tldr: This study quantitatively demonstrates that galaxy protoclusters at z > 2 significantly enhance X-ray AGN incidence among dusty star-forming galaxies by ~2.7x compared to field samples, driven by environmental factors beyond host galaxy properties.
AI.motivation: Super-massive black hole growth in dense protocluster environments at high redshift remains unclear due to heterogeneous galaxy selections and AGN identification methods in prior work.
AI.method: ALMA-detected DSFGs in seven protoclusters at 2 < z < 4.5 were compared to a selection-matched control sample from COSMOS; X-ray AGN incidence and host galaxy properties were statistically analyzed via uniform SED fitting.
AI.result: X-ray AGN fraction is enhanced by ~2.7x in protoclusters (p=3e-4), consistent across redshift bins (2-3 and 3-4.5), with matched stellar mass, SFR, and dust mass ruling out selection biases.
AI.conclusion: Dense protocluster environments promote SMBH growth in DSFGs beyond what host properties predict, likely via enhanced gas availability and interaction-driven fueling.

title: Metal-Poor Gas Accretion Drives Giant Clump Formation at 0.6 < z < 2.6
comment: 16 pages, 7 figures, submitted to ApJ
summary: The physical properties of kiloparsec-scale clumps in high-redshift star-forming galaxies (SFGs) contain crucial constraints on how they assemble. Building on recent work that indicates the presence of a metallicity offset in clumpy galaxies compared to nonclumpy SFGs, we analyze the chemical abundance in a large sample of ${\sim}300$ SFGs between $0.6<z<2.6$ using LEGA-C, MOSDEF and CANUCS near-infrared spectroscopic observations. We find that clumpy galaxies generally have lower gas-phase metallcities compared to the mass-metallicity relation, while nonclumpy galaxies have higher metallicities. We further investigate the relationship between the resolved stellar properties of clumps and the integrated gas-phase metallicity of the host galaxies using a subset of galaxies observed in the CANUCS fields. In particular, clumps in SFGs with metallicity below the mass-metallicity relation (i.e., $ΔZ \leq 0$) are generally younger and have higher SFRs, compared to clumps whose host galaxies have $ΔZ > 0$. We do not find a significant mass difference between these two clump populations. Finally, we compute the merger statistic using the Gini-M20 morphological parameters and find that the majority of clumpy galaxies are not classified as mergers based on their stellar mass maps. The results suggest that the clumpy nature of cosmic noon galaxies is linked to metal-poor gas accretion events that trigger star formation and dilute metallicities.

AI.tldr: Analysis of ~300 star-forming galaxies at z=0.6-2.6 shows clumpy galaxies have lower metallicities than the mass-metallicity relation, while nonclumpy galaxies have higher metallicities. Clumps in metal-poor hosts are younger and have higher SFRs. Most clumpy galaxies are not mergers, suggesting metal-poor gas accretion drives clump formation.
AI.motivation: To understand how kiloparsec-scale clumps in high-redshift star-forming galaxies assemble by constraining their physical properties, building on evidence of a metallicity offset in clumpy galaxies.
AI.method: Analyzed chemical abundances in ~300 SFGs at 0.6<z<2.6 using LEGA-C, MOSDEF, and CANUCS NIR spectroscopy; compared clumpy vs. nonclumpy galaxies relative to the mass-metallicity relation; studied resolved stellar properties of clumps and host galaxy metallicities; used Gini-M20 morphological parameters for merger classification.
AI.result: Clumpy galaxies have lower gas-phase metallicities compared to the mass-metallicity relation. Clumps in metal-poor hosts (ΔZ ≤ 0) are younger and have higher SFRs than those in metal-rich hosts. No significant mass difference between clump populations. Most clumpy galaxies are not classified as mergers.
AI.conclusion: The clumpy nature of cosmic noon galaxies is linked to metal-poor gas accretion events that trigger star formation and dilute metallicities, rather than being primarily driven by merger activity.

title: Dynamical models of cluster members to probe the total mass properties of cluster subhalos. I. A comparison with parametric strong lensing models
comment: 17 pages, 15 figures, 4 tables. Accepted for publication in A&A
summary: In this series of papers, we present dynamical models of cluster members in strong lensing (SL) galaxy clusters to independently probe the persistent discrepancy reported between SL models and cosmological simulations, in terms of total mass properties for the cluster subhalos. In this work, we focused our study on early-type galaxies within Abell 2744 ($z=0.309$) and MACS J0416.1-2403 ($z=0.397$). We took advantage of deep MUSE spectroscopic data, complemented with HFF photometry. We used a pipeline based on spectral fitting to perform kinematic measurements of the LOS velocity dispersion profiles of 109 cluster members. We modeled the galaxies assuming a dPIE total mass density distribution and a Jaffe stellar mass density distribution. From the models, we inferred the values of the central stellar velocity dispersion, $σ_0$, and the truncation radius, $r_t$, for the galaxies in our sample. We found that $σ_0$ is accurately recovered for all of the cluster members, while $r_t$ is reliably measured for a fraction of galaxies in our sample, with sufficiently extended radial kinematic coverage. Our dynamical models predicted LOS velocity dispersion profiles that fit the measured ones better than those inferred from SL models. We then exploited the $σ_0$ measurements obtained from the dynamical models to calibrate the Faber-Jackson scaling relations for the cluster members in both galaxy clusters. When comparing our relations to those obtained in previous kinematics and SL works, we found systematically higher normalization and compatible slope and scatter values. We conclude that our dynamical measurements of $σ_0$ and $r_t$, along with calibrated scaling relations, are more robust than previous kinematic estimates which are biased by not taking into account the effects of the PSF, and should therefore be adopted as improved initial prescriptions in future SL models.

AI.tldr: This paper presents dynamical models of early-type galaxies in two strong lensing clusters (Abell 2744 and MACS J0416.1-2403) using MUSE spectroscopy to measure velocity dispersion profiles. The models recover central stellar velocity dispersion (σ₀) accurately for all 109 cluster members and truncation radius (r_t) for a subset with sufficient kinematic coverage. The dynamical models outperform SL models in fitting observed LOS velocity dispersion profiles. Calibrated Faber-Jackson relations show systematically higher normalization but compatible slope and scatter compared to previous SL and kinematic works. The authors conclude their σ₀ and r_t measurements are more robust than prior kinematic estimates and should inform future SL models.
AI.motivation: To independently probe the persistent discrepancy between strong lensing models and cosmological simulations regarding total mass properties of cluster subhalos, by presenting dynamical models of cluster members in strong lensing galaxy clusters.
AI.method: Used deep MUSE spectroscopic data complemented with HFF photometry; applied a spectral-fitting pipeline to measure LOS velocity dispersion profiles of 109 cluster members; modeled galaxies assuming a dPIE total mass density distribution and a Jaffe stellar mass density distribution to infer σ₀ and r_t; calibrated Faber-Jackson scaling relations from the dynamical σ₀ measurements.
AI.result: σ₀ accurately recovered for all cluster members; r_t reliably measured only for galaxies with sufficiently extended radial kinematic coverage; dynamical models fit LOS velocity dispersion profiles better than SL models; calibrated Faber-Jackson relations show systematically higher normalization but compatible slope and scatter compared to previous works.
AI.conclusion: Dynamical measurements of σ₀ and r_t, along with calibrated scaling relations, are more robust than previous kinematic estimates (which were biased by PSF effects) and should be adopted as improved initial prescriptions in future strong lensing models.

title: The free-streaming length of dark matter from JWST observations of 28 strong gravitational lenses
comment: accepted by PRL
summary: The formation of gravitationally bound overdensities of dark matter (DM), or \textit{halos}, is a generic prediction of theories with particle DM. We present a measurement of halo properties in 28 quadruple image strong lens systems recently observed by JWST, and use these observations to constrain the free-streaming length, $λ_{\rm{FS}}$, of DM, a quantity that depends on the DM particle mass and formation mechanism. We improve on previous lensing analyses by simultaneously reconstructing extended lensed arcs with image positions and relative magnifications, enhancing sensitivity to perturbations by halos. Our analysis rules out deviations from the predictions of cold dark matter (CDM) on scales above $10^{7.2} M_{\odot}$ and $10^{7.4} M_{\odot}$ for subhalo abundance predicted by cosmological $N$-body simulations and semi-analytic models, respectively. These bounds correspond to upper limits $λ_{\rm{FS}}<6.0 \ \rm{kpc}$ and $λ_{\rm{FS}}<7.0 \ \rm{kpc}$, and lower limits on the mass of a spin--1/2 thermal relic DM particle $m_{\rm{therm}}>7.4 \ \rm{keV}$ and $m_{\rm{therm}}>6.5 \ \rm{keV}$. Conversely, assuming a negligible free-streaming length, as predicted by CDM, we measure a projected mass in subhalos around elliptical galaxies $1.7_{-1.2}^{+2.6} \times 10^7 \ \mathrm{M}_{\odot} \ \rm{kpc^{-2}}$ at $95 \%$ confidence. These inferences confirm key predictions of the CDM paradigm.

AI.tldr: Using 28 JWST strong lens systems, the paper constrains DM free-streaming length to λ_FS < 6-7 kpc and thermal relic mass > 6.5-7.4 keV, ruling out deviations from CDM above ~10^7 M⊙.
AI.motivation: To test predictions of particle DM theories by measuring halo properties in strong lens systems and constraining the free-streaming length of DM, which reflects particle mass and formation mechanism.
AI.method: Simultaneous reconstruction of extended lensed arcs, image positions, and relative magnifications in 28 quadruple-image strong lens systems observed by JWST, improving sensitivity to halo perturbations compared to previous analyses.
AI.result: Rules out CDM deviations above 10^7.2 M⊙ (N-body) and 10^7.4 M⊙ (semi-analytic); λ_FS < 6.0 kpc and < 7.0 kpc; m_therm > 7.4 keV and > 6.5 keV; subhalo projected mass 1.7_{-1.2}^{+2.6} × 10^7 M⊙ kpc^{-2} at 95% confidence.
AI.conclusion: The results confirm key predictions of the CDM paradigm.

title: A Decade to Map the Diffuse Universe: FRB-QSO Pairs with HST/COS Spectroscopy
comment: 5 pages, 1 figure; White Paper submitted to STScI and NASA GSFC in response to "Building a Roadmap for Hubble Science into the 2030s"
summary: Jointly analyzing the sightlines of arcsecond-localized fast radio bursts (FRBs) and UV-bright quasars (QSOs) nearby in projection has the potential to provide strong constraints on the phases, mass distributions, and magnetic structure of the diffuse universe. Each probe supplies what the other cannot: FRBs provide integrated electron columns (DM), line-of-sight magnetic field estimates (RM), and scattering constraints ($τ_{\rm scatt}$) that are independent of gas phase; QSOs provide the redshift- and phase-resolved column densities needed to interpret them. Today, there are only $\sim100$ arcsecond-localized FRBs at $z < 1$, making statistical FRB-QSO pair surveys impossible. By 2035, there will be $\sim10^{5}$. Using the most recent FRB localization forecasts and UV-bright QSO catalogs, we estimate that next-generation interferometers will yield thousands of FRB--QSO pairs at angular separations $θ< 10'$, including $\sim100$ pairs at $θ< 1'$, over a common 20,000\,deg$^2$ footprint by 2035. We outline the science enabled by this sample: constraints on CGM ionization fractions and baryon masses; observational constraints on the role of magnetic fields and turbulence in the CGM and cosmic web; sightline-by-sightline partitioning of the cosmic DM budget; and three-dimensional mapping of the multiphase Milky Way and M31 halos. Together, these measurements directly address the physics of feedback, non-thermal pressure support, and energy balance in the diffuse gas that regulates galaxy growth. HST/COS is the only instrument that can carry out this program, and the 2030s are the only decade in which to do it before Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) defines the next era of diffuse universe science.

AI.tldr: The paper forecasts that by 2035, next-generation interferometers will yield thousands of FRB–QSO pairs (including ~100 at <1') over 20,000 deg², enabling joint analysis of FRB dispersion/rotation measures with QSO absorption-line data to constrain CGM physics, cosmic web magnetic fields, and the diffuse universe's baryon and energy budget—a program uniquely feasible with HST/COS in the 2030s before HWO.
AI.motivation: Joint analysis of arcsecond-localized FRBs and UV-bright QSOs can provide powerful constraints on diffuse gas phases, mass distributions, and magnetic structure, but current samples (~100 FRBs at z<1) are too small for statistical pair surveys. The upcoming dramatic increase in FRB localizations (~10⁵ by 2035) motivates forecasting the feasibility and science potential of FRB–QSO pair studies.
AI.method: The authors combine the most recent FRB localization forecasts with UV-bright QSO catalogs to estimate the number and angular separation distribution of FRB–QSO pairs achievable by next-generation interferometers over a common 20,000 deg² footprint by 2035.
AI.result: Next-generation interferometers will yield thousands of FRB–QSO pairs at θ<10' and ~100 pairs at θ<1' by 2035, enabling sightline-by-sightline joint analyses of DM, RM, scattering, and UV absorption-line data.
AI.conclusion: This FRB–QSO pair sample will enable constraints on CGM ionization fractions, baryon masses, magnetic fields and turbulence, partitioning of the cosmic DM budget, and 3D mapping of Milky Way and M31 halos—directly addressing feedback, non-thermal pressure support, and energy balance in diffuse gas. HST/COS is the only instrument capable of this program, and the 2030s are the unique decade to execute it before HWO defines the next era.

title: AGN Line-Intensity Mapping: A Probe of Faint Black Holes at Cosmic Noon
comment: 12 pages, 4 figures, submitted to JCAP
summary: We propose line-intensity mapping (LIM) as a new probe of active galactic nuclei (AGN). By cross-correlating [Ne V] intensity maps with galaxy redshift surveys, we show that the cumulative AGN line emission can be detected even when individual sources are below the detection threshold. The 97.1 eV ionization potential of [Ne V] makes it an essentially uncontaminated tracer of AGN activity, arising from the narrow line region which is accessible even in heavily obscured AGN. We forecast signal-to-noise ratios using a Fisher matrix formalism for two hypothetical future instruments: a CDIM-like instrument targeting [Ne V] $λ3426$ and a PRIMA-like instrument optimized for LIM targeting [Ne V] $14.3 μ$m. For the CDIM-like case we find strong constraints on the product of the mean AGN intensity and bias, $S_{\rm NeV} b_{\rm NeV}$, across $z=2-3$, with redshift-space distortions enabling individual constraints on $S_{\rm NeV}$ and $b_{\rm NeV}$. The LIM signal retains sensitivity to AGN below the $5σ$ direct detection threshold, which at $z=3$ corresponds to $L_{\rm bol} \sim 5\times10^{43}$ erg s$^{-1}$ and coincides with the faint end of existing luminosity function measurements. Roughly 10% of the total signal originates from below this threshold, with the sub-threshold population detectable at $S/N=9-4$ across $z=2-3$ (for $S_{\rm NeV} b_{\rm NeV}$). The PRIMA-like instrument achieves slightly lower signal-to-noise but provides a complementary probe of the AGN population due to the insensitivity of the $14.3 μ$m line to dust attenuation. AGN LIM can potentially be applied to several scientific problems including tracing the total AGN emissivity history, constraining the black hole-halo connection at faint luminosities, and discriminating between supermassive black hole seeding mechanisms.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes line-intensity mapping (LIM) of [Ne V] emission as a new probe of AGN activity, demonstrating through Fisher forecasts that cross-correlating [Ne V] intensity maps with galaxy surveys can detect cumulative AGN emission below individual detection thresholds across z=2-3, with applications to AGN emissivity, black hole-halo connection, and SMBH seeding.
AI.motivation: To develop a novel observational probe (LIM) that can detect AGN activity below the direct detection threshold, especially for heavily obscured AGN, using [Ne V] as an uncontaminated tracer due to its high ionization potential (97.1 eV).
AI.method: Cross-correlation of [Ne V] line-intensity maps (targeting λ3426 and 14.3 μm) with galaxy redshift surveys, analyzed via Fisher matrix formalism to forecast signal-to-noise ratios for two hypothetical instruments (CDIM-like and PRIMA-like).
AI.result: CDIM-like instrument provides strong constraints on S_NeV * b_NeV across z=2-3, with redshift-space distortions enabling separate constraints on intensity and bias. The sub-threshold AGN population (below 5σ direct detection, L_bol ~ 5×10^43 erg/s at z=3) contributes ~10% of total signal and is detectable at S/N=9-4. PRIMA-like yields slightly lower S/N but offers dust-insensitive complementary constraints via the 14.3 μm line.
AI.conclusion: AGN LIM is a viable new probe with applications to tracing AGN emissivity history, constraining black hole-halo connection at faint luminosities, and discriminating between SMBH seeding mechanisms.

title: Strong [OIII]$+$H$β$ emitters dominated the ionizing budget at $z\sim7$
comment: 15 pages, 10 figures, 3 tables; submitted to ApJ
summary: We quantify the ionizing photon production at $z\sim7$ using the deepest spectroscopically confirmed sample of strong [OIII]$+$H$β$ emitters (rest-frame EW$>740$ A) in the Abell 2744 field. Leveraging ultra-deep UNCOVER F410M imaging ($5σ\sim29$ AB) and gravitational lensing, we probe an order of magnitude deeper than previous JWST WFSS [OIII] studies, reaching a luminosity limit of $\log(L_{\rm{[OIII]}+\rm{H}β}/\text{erg s}^{-1})=41.3$. Our rest-frame optical emission-line selection probes some of the youngest, metal- and dust-poor galaxies, identifying a large population of continuum-faint, ionizing candidates. NIRSpec follow-up of a luminosity-representative subset confirms $72\%$ of targets, providing detailed characterization of 18 emitters. Balmer decrements reveal negligible dust, while strong-line diagnostics indicate extremely low metallicities ($12+\log(\text{O/H})=6.8\text{--}7.7$). With typical [OII]/[OIII] ratios of $0.054\pm0.007$, we infer an average Lyman continuum escape fraction near the canonical $f_{\text{esc}}=20\%$. Correcting for the spectroscopic confirmation rate, we find that these high-EW emitters represent $56\pm12\%$ of the total UV-selected population by number density. Integrated to our survey limits, the ionizing budget of these emitters ($\log(\dot{N}_{\rm ion}/{\rm s}^{-1}\,\text{Mpc}^{-3})=50.63\pm0.05$) accounts for $\sim70\%$ of the total budget required for reionization at $z\sim7$. This result is consistent with empirical benchmarks. These results establish [OIII]$+$H$β$ selection as a powerful, dust-insensitive probe, showing that known galaxy populations significantly power reionization.

AI.tldr: This paper quantifies the ionizing photon production at z~7 using ultra-deep JWST observations of strong [OIII]+Hβ emitters in the Abell 2744 field. With NIRSpec confirmation, they find these emitters contribute ~70% of the total ionizing budget required for reionization, establishing [OIII]+Hβ selection as a powerful dust-insensitive probe of early galaxies.
AI.motivation: To quantify the ionizing photon production at z~7 and determine whether known galaxy populations can account for cosmic reionization, using a dust-insensitive selection method that probes young, metal-poor galaxies.
AI.method: Using ultra-deep JWST UNCOVER F410M imaging (5σ~29 AB) with gravitational lensing in Abell 2744, they selected strong [OIII]+Hβ emitters (rest-frame EW>740 Å) down to log(L)=41.3. NIRSpec follow-up confirmed 72% of targets and provided detailed characterization via Balmer decrements and strong-line diagnostics for 18 emitters.
AI.result: The emitters show negligible dust (Balmer decrements), extremely low metallicities (12+log(O/H)=6.8–7.7), and [OII]/[OIII]=0.054±0.007 implying f_esc~20%. They constitute 56±12% of the UV-selected population and produce an ionizing budget of log(ṅ_ion)=50.63±0.05, accounting for ~70% of the total required for reionization at z~7.
AI.conclusion: [OIII]+Hβ selection is a powerful dust-insensitive probe of early galaxies, and known galaxy populations significantly power cosmic reionization at z~7, consistent with empirical benchmarks.

title: The DESI results impact the local determination of $H_0$
comment: 5 pages, 4 figures
summary: Measurements of baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) by the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) have revealed evidence for dark energy that evolves. If local distance measurements are analyzed with the $w_0w_a$ models preferred by the DESI measurements, the value for the Hubble constant can be as much as $2.5\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}Mpc^{-1}}$ smaller than the value obtained assuming $Λ$CDM. When these $w_0w_a$ models are further constrained by cosmic microwave background (CMB) and type Ia supernova (SNIa) data, the downward shift is $1.1 \pm 0.38\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}Mpc^{-1}}$ (DESI + CMB) and $0.5 \pm 0.1\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}Mpc^{-1}}$ (DESI + CMB + SNIa). The dependence of local determinations of $H_0$ on the background cosmology, combined with the fact that the low-redshift cosmology is not well constrained, is relevant to the Hubble tension.

AI.tldr: The Hubble constant inferred from local distance measurements is sensitive to the assumed dark energy model. Using $w_0w_a$ models favored by DESI BAO data reduces $H_0$ by up to $2.5\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}Mpc^{-1}}$ compared to $\Lambda$CDM. With additional CMB/SNIa constraints, the shift is smaller but still significant, highlighting cosmology dependence as a factor in the Hubble tension.
AI.motivation: To investigate how the choice of dark energy model ($w_0w_a$ vs. $\Lambda$CDM) affects local measurements of the Hubble constant, and whether this cosmology dependence can alleviate the Hubble tension.
AI.method: Local distance measurements are reanalyzed under $w_0w_a$ dark energy models preferred by DESI BAO data, and further constrained by CMB and SNIa datasets. The resulting $H_0$ values are compared to those obtained under standard $\Lambda$CDM.
AI.result: Using $w_0w_a$ models alone shifts $H_0$ down by up to $2.5\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}Mpc^{-1}}$. With additional CMB constraints, the downward shift is $1.1 \pm 0.38\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}Mpc^{-1}}$; adding SNIa further reduces it to $0.5 \pm 0.1\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}Mpc^{-1}}$.
AI.conclusion: Local $H_0$ determinations depend on the assumed background cosmology; given that low-redshift cosmology is not well constrained, this dependence is relevant to the Hubble tension and may partially reconcile local and early-universe measurements.

title: Bulk vs. turbulent motions at the centres of galaxy clusters: AGN-driven turbulence according to TNG-Cluster
comment: 24 Pages, 17 figures. Comments welcomed. Submitted to MNRAS
summary:
The highly dynamic intracluster medium (ICM) influences cluster thermodynamic evolution and probes key physical processes. Quantifying the non-thermal motions is therefore essential for understanding cluster physics and interpreting high spectral-resolution X-ray observations from telescopes like {\it XRISM}.
  We quantify bulk and turbulent gas motions in 352 galaxy clusters at $z=0$ (${\rm M_{200c}=10^{14.3-15.4}\, M_\odot}$) from the TNG-Cluster suite of magneto-hydrodynamical galaxy simulations. We use a multi-scale filtering Reynolds decomposition to separate total gas velocities into bulk (coherent) and turbulent (small-scale fluctuations) components. We primarily focus on the hot X-ray emitting gas in the central core regions.
  According to TNG-Cluster, majority of the ICM has subsonic turbulence but with broad velocity distributions reaching $\mathcal{M}_{\rm Turb}\sim 10$ and large cluster-to-cluster variations. In cluster centres, turbulence contributes less than half of the total velocity dispersion $(σ_{v\rm,Turb } \sim 0.5 ~σ_{v,\rm Total})$ for most clusters, with typical turbulent velocity dispersions of $50-75$ km s$^{-1}$ across the mass range, and with sub per cent levels of turbulent pressure support. Clusters that are strong cool cores, or have X-ray cavities, or experienced recent SMBH feedback energy injections exhibit systematically larger turbulent velocity dispersions and more prominent turbulent velocity tails. On average, the turbulent velocity dispersion peaks in cluster centres, decreases slightly to a minimum at $0.1-0.2 \, R_{\rm500c}$, then rises again.
  Our analysis shows that SMBH feedback is a key driver of turbulence in cluster cores, generating strong but short-lived motion alongside high-velocity outflows. It also calls for caution for interpreting {\it XRISM} observations.

AI.tldr: This study quantifies bulk and turbulent gas motions in 352 galaxy clusters from TNG-Cluster simulations, finding that ICM turbulence is generally subsonic but highly variable, with turbulent velocity dispersions of 50-75 km/s in cluster cores and SMBH feedback as a key driver of turbulence.
AI.motivation: Quantifying non-thermal motions in the intracluster medium (ICM) is essential for understanding cluster thermodynamic evolution, key physical processes, and interpreting high spectral-resolution X-ray observations from telescopes like XRISM.
AI.method: Analyzed 352 galaxy clusters at z=0 (M200c=10^14.3-15.4 M⊙) from TNG-Cluster magneto-hydrodynamical simulations, using multi-scale filtering Reynolds decomposition to separate bulk (coherent) and turbulent (small-scale) velocity components, focusing on hot X-ray emitting gas in core regions.
AI.result: ICM has subsonic turbulence with broad velocity distributions (ℳ_Turb∼10) and large cluster-to-cluster variations. Turbulence contributes <50% of total velocity dispersion in most cluster centers (σ_v,Turb∼0.5σ_v,Total), with typical turbulent dispersions of 50-75 km/s and sub-percent turbulent pressure support. Strong cool cores, X-ray cavities, or recent SMBH feedback show larger turbulence. Turbulent velocity dispersion peaks at centers, dips at 0.1-0.2 R500c, then rises.
AI.conclusion: SMBH feedback is a key driver of turbulence in cluster cores, generating strong but short-lived motion with high-velocity outflows. Results call for caution in interpreting XRISM observations.

title: On the potential for inhomogeneities to mimic an evolving dark energy
comment: 14 pages, 7 figures, submitted to PRD. Comments welcome
summary: In this work we explore the ability of inhomogeneities to result in an apparent dynamical evolution of dark energy. The idea that inhomogeneities may alter the expansion history of the Universe is not a new one. However, with the current excitement surrounding the inferred time-evolution of the equation of state of dark energy by the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), combined with Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) and supernovae observations, it is worth revisiting. We use numerical relativity simulations of large-scale structure formation combined with nonlinear general-relativistic ray tracing to infer dark energy parameters for synthetic observers. We adopt a simplified set-up to roughly mimic the observational properties of the DESI plus supernovae and CMB constraints. In our small sample of 20 observers, we find one who infers parameters consistent with the DESI values at 2-$σ$ significance. While it is rare in our limited sample size, we show that it is at least possible for observers to infer significant non-LCDM parameters when their universe is well-described by a cosmological constant on average.

AI.tldr: This paper uses numerical relativity simulations with ray tracing to show that cosmic inhomogeneities can cause some observers to infer evolving dark energy (like DESI results) even when the universe's average behavior is LCDM with a cosmological constant.
AI.motivation: The recent DESI data suggests possible time-evolution of dark energy's equation of state, motivating a re-examination of whether cosmic inhomogeneities (rather than actual dynamical dark energy) could produce such apparent signals.
AI.method: Numerical relativity simulations of large-scale structure formation combined with nonlinear general-relativistic ray tracing were used to infer dark energy parameters for 20 synthetic observers, with a simplified set-up mimicking DESI, supernovae, and CMB observational constraints.
AI.result: Out of 20 simulated observers, one inferred dark energy parameters consistent with DESI values at 2-σ significance, despite the underlying universe being LCDM (cosmological constant) on average.
AI.conclusion: It is possible for observers in an LCDM universe to infer apparent dynamical dark energy parameters due to inhomogeneities, though this is rare (at least in the limited sample size of 20).

title: A Kinematic Study of Wolf-Rayet Stars at the Galactic Center I: Binary Candidates and Constraints on the Binary Fraction
comment: Submitted to ApJ, in review
summary: We report the binary fraction of Wolf-Rayet (WR) stars within 0.5~pc of the Galactic center obtained through the longest time-baseline (1994-2024) kinematic study of this population of stars. The new radial velocity ($v_{z}$) data we present is primarily from the W. M. Keck Observatory, with additional $v_{z}$ measurements from Gemini North Observatory. When combining our new $v_{z}$ measurements with literature measurements, we find $v_{z}$ variations suggesting the presence of a companion for five out of 27 WR stars, of which two are newly identified here (IRS~13E4, S8-181), along with three previously detected binaries (IRS~16SW, IRS~16NE, S4-258). Based on our experimental sensitivity and expected properties of the underlying population, we infer the binary fraction of the WR stars in the Galactic center to be 0.56$\pm$0.18. This is consistent with previous photometric studies of the young stars in the Galactic center, and with the binary fraction of field WR stars. When our results are combined with the results of previous photometric work, we find a binary fraction of 0.69$\pm$0.17 for the WR stars in the Galactic center.

AI.tldr: A 30-year (1994-2024) kinematic study of Wolf-Rayet stars within 0.5 pc of the Galactic center, using Keck and Gemini data, finds radial velocity variations indicating binaries in 5 out of 27 WR stars (2 newly identified, 3 previously known), yielding a binary fraction of 0.56±0.18, consistent with field WR stars and prior photometric studies.
AI.motivation: To determine the binary fraction of Wolf-Rayet stars in the Galactic center through long-baseline kinematic monitoring, which is critical for understanding stellar evolution, mass loss, and the production of compact object binaries in this extreme environment.
AI.method: Longest time-baseline (1994-2024) radial velocity kinematic study using W. M. Keck Observatory (primary) and Gemini North Observatory (supplementary) data, combined with literature measurements to identify v_z variations indicative of binarity. Experimental sensitivity and expected population properties were used to infer the binary fraction.
AI.result: 5 out of 27 WR stars show v_z variations suggesting companions: 2 newly identified (IRS 13E4, S8-181) and 3 previously known (IRS 16SW, IRS 16NE, S4-258). Inferred binary fraction = 0.56±0.18; combined with prior photometric work yields 0.69±0.17.
AI.conclusion: The Galactic center WR binary fraction (~0.56-0.69) is consistent with that of field WR stars and previous photometric studies of young stars in the region.

title: Dissipative Cosmology and the Nature of Dark Energy: Insights from Bulk Viscosity with DESI DR2 observations
comment: 20 pages, 7 figures
summary: We explore a cosmological model in which dark energy is described by a bulk viscous fluid, providing a dissipative mechanism for late-time cosmic acceleration. Considering both minimally and non-minimally coupled scenarios, we constrain the model using SNe Ia, DESI DR2 BAO, and Planck 2018 CMB data. We find that viscous effects can successfully mimic dynamical dark energy and yield improved fits over $Λ$CDM, particularly in the interacting non-minimal case. Our results demonstrate that dissipative processes offer a viable and physically motivated alternative to the cosmological constant in explaining the current accelerated expansion of the universe.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates a bulk viscous fluid model of dark energy, finding that viscous dissipation can mimic dynamical dark energy and provide improved fits to SNe Ia, DESI DR2 BAO, and Planck 2018 CMB data compared to ΛCDM, especially in the non-minimally coupled interacting scenario.
AI.motivation: To explore whether dissipative (bulk viscous) processes can serve as a physically motivated alternative to the cosmological constant for explaining late-time cosmic acceleration.
AI.method: A bulk viscous fluid dark energy model is considered in both minimally and non-minimally coupled scenarios, and constrained using SNe Ia, DESI DR2 BAO, and Planck 2018 CMB data.
AI.result: Viscous effects can successfully mimic dynamical dark energy; the model yields improved fits over ΛCDM, particularly in the interacting non-minimal coupling case.
AI.conclusion: Dissipative processes offer a viable and physically motivated alternative to the cosmological constant for explaining cosmic acceleration.

title: A linear residual structure across galaxy rotation curves
comment: 8 pages 3 figures, SI included
summary: Galaxy rotation curves have long indicated that the observed motions of stars and gas cannot be fully explained by visible matter alone. Here we investigate the residual component that remains after subtraction of the baryonic contribution. Using galaxies from the SPARC and LITTLE THINGS surveys, we find that the residuals are not randomly distributed but instead follow a common linear pattern across a diverse galaxy population. The residual structure separates into a mass-coupled component and a nearly mass-independent component. These empirical regularities provide new constraints on theories of galaxy dynamics.

AI.tldr: Analysis of galaxy rotation curve residuals reveals a common linear pattern after subtracting baryonic contributions, splitting into mass-coupled and mass-independent components, providing new constraints for galaxy dynamics theories.
AI.motivation: Galaxy rotation curves show motions that cannot be explained by visible matter alone, motivating investigation into the residual (non-baryonic) component to understand what drives these observed motions.
AI.method: Using galaxies from SPARC and LITTLE THINGS surveys, the baryonic contribution is subtracted from rotation curves, and the resulting residuals are analyzed for patterns across diverse galaxy populations.
AI.result: Residuals are not randomly distributed but follow a common linear pattern across diverse galaxies. The residual structure separates into a mass-coupled component and a nearly mass-independent component.
AI.conclusion: These empirical regularities provide new constraints on theories of galaxy dynamics, implying that any successful theory must reproduce this specific residual structure.

title: Metastability in Emergent Dark Energy: A New Framework Confronting Cosmological Observations
comment: 10 pages, 4 figures
summary: We propose the Metastable Emergent Dark Energy (MEDE) model, a novel phenomenological extension of the Phenomenological (PEDE) and Generalized (GEDE) Emergent Dark Energy frameworks, in which dark energy exhibits a transitionary behavior, appearing at late times and vanishing toward the future. This model naturally enables a smooth crossing of the phantom divide line in the dark energy equation of state, as hinted at by recent observations. The MEDE model is defined by a hyperbolic tangent dark energy equation of state $w(z)=-1-Δ\tanh[\log_{10}((1+z)/(1+z_t))]$, introducing only two free parameters, the transition redshift $z_t$ and the variation amplitude $Δ$, allowing both the emergent and transitionary behavior of dark energy. We constrain the MEDE model using a combined dataset of Planck CMB, DESI DR2 BAO, and different compilations of Type Ia supernovae, obtaining $z_t=0.425^{+0.084}_{-0.120}$ and $Δ=0.87^{+0.29}_{-0.35}$ (for CMB+DESI+PantheonPlus), indicating a statistically significant deviation from the cosmological constant. Statistical comparisons show that the MEDE model is preferred over $Λ$CDM by the combined dataset, with $Δ\rm DIC_{ MEDE-ΛCDM}= -9.29$. The MEDE model performs comparably to the CPL dynamical dark energy parametrization ($Δ\rm DIC_{MEDE-CPL} = 0.74$), with no strong statistical distinction from CPL using current data. Notably, MEDE preserves the success of $Λ$CDM in describing early-universe physics and naturally accommodates the phantom-crossing signature indicated by the latest low-redshift observations. The MEDE scenario provides a compelling dark energy phenomenology that may guide us toward interesting theoretical implications.

AI.tldr: The Metastable Emergent Dark Energy (MEDE) model introduces a hyperbolic tangent parameterization of dark energy's equation of state that enables phantom divide crossing, fits observational data (CMB+DESI+SNe) with $z_t=0.425^{+0.084}_{-0.120}$ and $\Delta=0.87^{+0.29}_{-0.35}$, and is statistically preferred over $\Lambda$CDM ($\Delta\mathrm{DIC}=-9.29$) while performing comparably to CPL.
AI.motivation: Observational hints of phantom crossing in dark energy's equation of state motivate a phenomenological model that extends beyond $\Lambda$CDM and existing emergent dark energy frameworks, allowing dark energy to appear at late times and vanish toward the future while naturally crossing the phantom divide ($w=-1$).
AI.method: The MEDE model defines $w(z) = -1 - \Delta \tanh[\log_{10}((1+z)/(1+z_t))]$, with two free parameters: transition redshift $z_t$ and amplitude $\Delta$. It is constrained using combined datasets: Planck CMB, DESI DR2 BAO, and multiple Type Ia supernova compilations (PantheonPlus).
AI.result: Constraints yield $z_t=0.425^{+0.084}_{-0.120}$ and $\Delta=0.87^{+0.29}_{-0.35}$ (CMB+DESI+PantheonPlus), indicating significant deviation from $\Lambda$CDM. MEDE is preferred over $\Lambda$CDM ($\Delta\mathrm{DIC}=-9.29$) and performs comparably to CPL ($\Delta\mathrm{DIC}=0.74$).
AI.conclusion: MEDE provides a compelling dark energy phenomenology that preserves early-universe $\Lambda$CDM success, naturally accommodates phantom-crossing signatures from low-redshift data, and may guide theoretical developments beyond the standard model.

title: Mapping Active Star-Formation in Serpens and the Aquila Rift
comment: Accepted, AJ
summary: We report the results of a high-sensitivity survey for Herbig-Haro (HH) outflows in the Serpens-Aquila Rift using the DECam instrument on the 4-meter telescope. We have detected 88 new HH objects, more than tripling the total known in this region. We have also identified likely progenitors for most of these outflows. By combining HH object and progenitor locations with literature dust maps and Gaia astrometry, we find that HH objects mark five spatially distinct clouds hosting active star formation: the Serpens Molecular Cloud and LDN 673 at 400-500 pc, the more distant West and East components of the Aquila Rift at ~600 and 700 pc, respectively, and a near cloud in Serpens at ~250 pc. In both the Serpens Molecular Cloud and the Western Aquila Rift, HH objects broadly trace gas structures on the edges of low-density cavities surrounding known stellar populations, consistent with active star formation in feedback-driven shells. The near cloud in Serpens is not associated with any established stellar population, but its position and velocity suggest that it is part of the Local Bubble. And the HH objects there may mark the start of a new stellar generation connected to the Scutum North Association. Our Herbig-Haro objects therefore serve as a powerful indicator of star formation sites even in the absence of astrometrically characterized young stars, making them a useful tool for guiding future YSO surveys.

AI.tldr: A high-sensitivity DECam survey in the Serpens-Aquila Rift discovered 88 new Herbig-Haro objects, tripling known counts, and identified five distinct star-forming clouds at varying distances (250-700 pc), with HH objects tracing feedback-driven shells and revealing a new nearby cloud linked to the Local Bubble.
AI.motivation: To conduct a high-sensitivity survey for Herbig-Haro outflows in the Serpens-Aquila Rift to map active star formation sites, identify their progenitors, and use HH objects as indicators of star formation independent of astrometrically characterized young stars.
AI.method: Survey using the DECam instrument on the 4-meter telescope to detect HH objects; combined HH and progenitor locations with literature dust maps and Gaia astrometry to identify distinct clouds and star-forming regions.
AI.result: Detected 88 new HH objects (tripling known total); identified likely progenitors for most outflows; distinguished five spatially distinct star-forming clouds (Serpens Molecular Cloud, LDN 673, West/East Aquila Rift, a near Serpens cloud); found HH objects trace gas on edges of low-density cavities around known stellar populations.
AI.conclusion: HH objects are powerful indicators of star formation sites even without astrometrically characterized young stars, making them a useful tool for guiding future YSO surveys.

title: Reconstructing dark energy with fewer assumptions
comment: 24 pages, 14 figures
summary: We perform minimalistic reconstructions of the dark energy density and equation of state using late-time distance measurements. Our methodology avoids assumptions that correlate the values of these functions over time and instead yields their approximate average evolution within seven redshift bins from $z=0$ to $z=4.2$. Constraints are obtained using combinations of BAO measurements from DESI and SDSS, alongside Type Ia supernovae measurements from Pantheon+ and the latest recalibrated samples, Union3.1 and DES-Dovekie. Only an acoustic scale prior is included from the CMB so that our results are insensitive to the possible matter density tension between early and late-time probes. All combinations yield consistent reconstructed histories: a dark energy density that rises to a local maximum before decreasing at late times and an equation of state with two apparent oscillations around the cosmological constant limit. Both functions tentatively suggest a phantom crossing in the equation of state around $z\sim0.6$-$0.8$. These patterns are robust to numerous parameter extensions, such as freely varying spatial curvature and neutrino mass, and they persist in the uncorrelated amplitudes obtained through localized principal component analysis. Deviations from $Λ$CDM in individual bins reach a maximum significance of $\sim2.6$-$3σ$, while the total chi-square difference between the reconstructions and this model provides up to $\sim2σ$ support for the seven additional parameters in the reconstructions. As these significances remain moderate, our main result is the level of consistency between combinations of the most widely used background-level observations. Our results suggest that the dark energy evolution signal is a persistent feature of the data and that it cannot be explained solely by fluctuations or systematics in individual measurements.

AI.tldr: The paper reconstructs dark energy density and equation of state in 7 redshift bins (z=0-4.2) using BAO (DESI, SDSS), supernovae (Pantheon+, Union3.1, DES-Dovekie), and CMB acoustic scale priors. Results show dark energy density peaking then decreasing, equation of state oscillating around ΛCDM with a phantom crossing at z~0.6-0.8, reaching ~2.6-3σ significance in individual bins and ~2σ overall support for extra parameters.
AI.motivation: To perform minimalistic, assumption-free reconstructions of dark energy properties (density and equation of state) across cosmic time using late-time distance measurements, avoiding parametric models that correlate values across redshifts, and to test whether deviations from ΛCDM are persistent features of the data or due to systematics.
AI.method: Reconstructed dark energy density and equation of state in 7 redshift bins (z=0 to 4.2) using combinations of BAO (DESI, SDSS), Type Ia supernovae (Pantheon+, Union3.1, DES-Dovekie), and a CMB acoustic scale prior. Used localized principal component analysis for uncorrelated amplitudes. Tested robustness by varying spatial curvature and neutrino mass freely.
AI.result: All data combinations consistently show: (1) dark energy density rising to a local maximum then decreasing at late times; (2) equation of state oscillating around ΛCDM with phantom crossing at z~0.6-0.8; (3) deviations from ΛCDM reach ~2.6-3σ in individual bins and ~2σ overall chi-square difference for 7 extra parameters; (4) patterns persist under parameter extensions (curvature, neutrino mass) and localized PCA.
AI.conclusion: The dark energy evolution signal is a persistent feature of the data, not explainable by fluctuations or systematics in individual measurements. However, significances remain moderate (≤3σ), so the main result is the consistency between different combinations of widely used background-level observations.

title: Evolution of the stellar mass function in open clusters from a universal and unsegregated initial state
comment: 8 pages, 2 figures, Accepted for publication in ApJ Letters
summary: The stellar mass function (MF) and its spatial variation (mass segregation) within star clusters encode signatures of early formation physics and subsequent secular evolution. Yet, a coherent evolutionary picture remains elusive due to conflicting reports regarding the universality of the initial mass function (IMF) and the prevalence of primordial mass segregation. These discrepancies often arise from unresolved binaries, field contamination, and completeness bias. Here, we resolve these issues by analyzing 163 high-fidelity open clusters via a Bayesian forward-modeling framework. We reveal a remarkably simple initial state: young clusters ($\lesssim 300$ Myr) share a mean IMF slope of $-2.29$ in the mass range $M \geq 0.5 M_\odot$, consistent with the Salpeter slope but with an intrinsic scatter of 0.17, and exhibit minimal mass segregation at the onset of gas-free evolution ($\sim$10 Myr). This broadly universal "zero-point" for secular evolution disfavors star-forming scenarios that predict strong primordial segregation or significant IMF variations, and suggests that chaotic cluster assembly and gas expulsion efficiently erase any mild primordial inhomogeneities. By tracing the evolutionary sequence from $10^7$ to $10^{9.8}$ yr, we demonstrate that dynamical processing operates on distinct timescales: mass segregation proceeds rapidly via internal relaxation, whereas global MF flattening due to tidal evaporation becomes dominant only after $\sim$600 Myr. These findings impose robust observational constraints on the physics of star formation and early feedback and establish an empirical baseline for modeling secular stellar dynamics.

AI.tldr: Analysis of 163 open clusters via Bayesian forward modeling reveals a universal IMF slope of −2.29 (Salpeter-like) with minimal primordial mass segregation in young clusters (≲300 Myr), and identifies distinct timescales for dynamical processing: rapid internal relaxation drives mass segregation, while tidal evaporation flattens the MF only after ~600 Myr.
AI.motivation: To resolve conflicting reports about the universality of the IMF and prevalence of primordial mass segregation in star clusters, which often stem from unresolved binaries, field contamination, and completeness bias.
AI.method: Bayesian forward-modeling framework applied to 163 high-fidelity open clusters, analyzing the stellar mass function and its spatial variation across ages from 10^7 to 10^9.8 yr.
AI.result: Young clusters (≲300 Myr) share a mean IMF slope of −2.29 (M ≥ 0.5 M⊙, intrinsic scatter 0.17) and exhibit minimal mass segregation at ~10 Myr. Dynamical processing is timescale-dependent: mass segregation via internal relaxation proceeds rapidly, while global MF flattening via tidal evaporation dominates after ~600 Myr.
AI.conclusion: The findings disfavor star-forming scenarios predicting strong primordial segregation or significant IMF variations, suggest chaotic cluster assembly and gas expulsion erase mild primordial inhomogeneities, and establish robust observational constraints for star formation physics and secular stellar dynamics modeling.

title: AKRA 3.0: A matrix-free Inversion Framework for Weak Lensing Mass Mapping and Its Application to DES Y3 Data
comment: 14 pages, 6 figures
summary:
Weak gravitational lensing mass mapping offers a direct probe of the matter distribution.
  Accurate reconstruction of mass maps from masked shear catalogs remains challenging due to survey boundaries and spatially varying noise. In AKRA 2.0, we addressed the mask problem on the curved sky by constructing and inverting the normal-equation matrix $\bf{H} \equiv \mathbf{A}^\mathrm{T}\mathbf{N}^{-1} \mathbf{A}$ explicitly, necessitating a split-scale strategy that reconstructed different angular scales independently to reach high resolution.
  Here we present AKRA 3.0, in which $\mathbf{H}$ is treated as a linear operator and the normal equations are solved by the conjugate gradient (CG) method. This reformulation reduces the memory requirement from $O(N^2)$ to $O(N)$ and the inversion cost from $O(N^3)$ to $O(N_{\rm iter}N^{3/2}), N \sim \ell_{\rm{max}}^2$ for full-sky (SHT-based) operations. Such optimizations render high-resolution full-sky reconstruction tractable for Stage~III and Stage~IV surveys.
  Applying AKRA 3.0 to the DES Y3 \texttt{METACALIBRATION} catalog, we produce the highest-resolution convergence map of this dataset to date at HEALPix $N_{\rm{nside}}= 2048$ without imposing any prior assumptions.
  We extract the convergence power spectrum directly from the reconstructed map and demonstrate that unbiased two-point measurements can be obtained directly from the reconstructed map. The reconstructed E-mode convergence map will be publicly released as data products to enable future studies of non-Gaussian statistics, higher-order moments, and cross-correlations with external datasets.

AI.tldr: AKRA 3.0 presents a computationally efficient method for gravitational lensing mass mapping on the curved sky, using conjugate gradient solvers to reduce memory and computational costs, enabling high-resolution full-sky reconstruction without prior assumptions. Applied to DES Y3 data, it produces the highest-resolution convergence map to date at Nside=2048 and demonstrates unbiased power spectrum extraction.
AI.motivation: Weak gravitational lensing mass mapping is a direct probe of matter distribution, but accurate reconstruction from masked shear catalogs is challenged by survey boundaries and spatially varying noise. Prior methods (AKRA 2.0) required explicit matrix inversion with O(N²) memory and O(N³) cost, limiting resolution and scalability for Stage III/IV surveys.
AI.method: AKRA 3.0 treats the normal-equation matrix H as a linear operator and solves the normal equations via the conjugate gradient (CG) method, replacing the explicit matrix inversion used in AKRA 2.0. This reduces memory from O(N²) to O(N) and inversion cost from O(N³) to O(N_iter N^{3/2}) for full-sky SHT-based operations.
AI.result: Applied to the DES Y3 METACALIBRATION catalog, AKRA 3.0 produces the highest-resolution convergence map of this dataset at HEALPix Nside=2048 with no prior assumptions. Unbiased E-mode power spectrum measurements are obtained directly from the reconstructed map.
AI.conclusion: AKRA 3.0 makes high-resolution full-sky reconstruction tractable for current and upcoming surveys. The reconstructed E-mode convergence map will be publicly released to enable studies of non-Gaussian statistics, higher-order moments, and cross-correlations with external datasets.

title: WISE Photometry of Galaxies within 10 Mpc
comment: Accepted for publication in The Astronomical Journal
summary:
For photometry of galaxies in the infrared that extend to very low surface brightnesses, it is necessary to observe with telescopes in space.
  WISE and NEOWISE provide sensitive all-sky access to mid-infrared flux from galaxies at 3.4mum (W1) and 4.6mum (W2) bands.
  This study is complemented by the availability of accurate Tip of the Red Giant Branch distances for a large fraction of the targets.
  In this work, photometry is assembled on a complete volume limited sample of galaxies between one and ten Mpc brighter than absolute magnitude -13 in the W1 band.
  Stellar masses are inferred from W1 fluxes and measured distances.
  While most of the galaxies are dwarfs, most of the stellar mass is concentrated in a small number of giants.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a complete volume-limited sample of nearby galaxies (1-10 Mpc, M_W1 < -13) using WISE/NEOWISE photometry and TRGB distances to measure stellar masses, finding that while most galaxies are dwarfs, most stellar mass resides in a few giants.
AI.motivation: Infrared galaxy photometry reaching very low surface brightnesses requires space-based telescopes; WISE and NEOWISE provide sensitive all-sky mid-infrared data, and TRGB distances enable accurate mass measurements for a volume-limited sample.
AI.method: Photometry from WISE/NEOWISE at 3.4μm (W1) and 4.6μm (W2) is used to assemble a complete volume-limited sample of galaxies between 1 and 10 Mpc brighter than absolute magnitude -13 in W1; stellar masses are inferred from W1 fluxes and measured TRGB distances.
AI.result: Most galaxies in the sample are dwarfs, but the majority of stellar mass is concentrated in a small number of giant galaxies.
AI.conclusion: Space-based infrared observations combined with accurate TRGB distances allow robust stellar mass measurements for a complete, volume-limited nearby galaxy sample, revealing a classic mass-concentration pattern where dwarfs dominate in number but giants dominate in mass.

title: The Atacama Cosmology Telescope: Probing new signatures of ultralight axions with gravitational lensing
summary: Ultralight axions (ULAs) are well-motivated dark matter particle candidates that arise in many extensions of the Standard Model of particle physics. ULAs with mass $m_\mathrm{a} \lesssim 10^{-27}$ eV have been strongly constrained by cosmic microwave background (CMB) observations in temperature and polarization. We fit recent measurements of gravitational lensing of the CMB from \textit{Planck}, the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) and the South Pole Telescope (SPT-3G) using a state-of-the-art simulation-calibrated nonlinear clustering model for ULAs. We derive the strongest constraints on ULAs in the mass range $10^{-26}\;\mathrm{eV}\leq m_\mathrm{a}\leq 10^{-24.5}\;\mathrm{eV}$. ULAs of this mass have been shown to alleviate tensions between inferences of the matter clustering if they compose a few percent of the total dark matter content of the Universe. We conclude that ULAs with a mass of $10^{-26}$ eV make up less than 1.5\% of the dark matter and $10^{-25}$ eV axions make less than 9\% (both at 95\% confidence level). We identify a slight preference for non-zero axion density at $10^{-24.5}$ eV at $2.1σ$. We find that the preference for ULAs is largely driven by a few data points and that further investigation of non-linear ULA physics is needed to confirm or rule out this signal.

AI.tldr: Using CMB lensing data from Planck, ACT, and SPT-3G with a simulation-calibrated nonlinear clustering model, the authors derive the strongest constraints on ultralight axions (ULAs) in the mass range 10⁻²⁶–10⁻²⁴·⁵ eV, finding ULAs at 10⁻²⁶ eV comprise <1.5% of dark matter and 10⁻²⁵ eV axions <9% (95% CL), with a slight 2.1σ preference for non-zero density at 10⁻²⁴·⁵ eV that is driven by a few data points.
AI.motivation: ULAs are well-motivated dark matter candidates, and previous CMB temperature/polarization constraints leave a mass window (10⁻²⁶–10⁻²⁴·⁵ eV) where ULAs could alleviate tensions in matter clustering inferences if they constitute a few percent of dark matter. This motivates a dedicated analysis using CMB lensing data to probe this region.
AI.method: The authors fit CMB gravitational lensing measurements from Planck, ACT, and SPT-3G using a state-of-the-art simulation-calibrated nonlinear clustering model for ULAs, enabling robust constraints in the previously under-explored mass range.
AI.result: Strongest constraints to date for ULAs in mass range 10⁻²⁶–10⁻²⁴·⁵ eV: <1.5% of DM at 10⁻²⁶ eV, <9% at 10⁻²⁵ eV (95% CL). A 2.1σ preference for non-zero axion density is found at 10⁻²⁴·⁵ eV, but driven by a few data points.
AI.conclusion: ULAs in the probed mass range are tightly constrained; the tentative preference at 10⁻²⁴·⁵ eV requires further investigation with improved nonlinear ULA modeling to confirm or rule out the signal.

title: Galaxy morphology dependent (black hole mass)-(velocity dispersion) relations: implications for gravitational wave forecasts and cosmological simulations
comment: 23 pages (including an Appendix for SCOPE). Submitted to MNRAS on the 13th of May, 2026
summary: The correlation between black hole mass, $M_{\rm bh}$, and stellar velocity dispersion, $σ_0$, is revisited using 137 galaxies with quantitative bar strengths and enhanced morphological awareness. Interpreted within the `Triangal' evolutionary framework, gas-rich and gas-poor assembly pathways emerge in the $M_{\rm bh}$--$σ_0$ diagram. To quantify these scaling relations, a versatile Bayesian hierarchical regression code, dubbed the Symmetric COvariance Population Estimator (SCOPE), is introduced. Unlike conditional estimators, SCOPE derives the intrinsic population covariance, natively accommodating asymmetric measurement errors while guaranteeing directional invariance between axes. Primeval, dust-poor S0 galaxies (including dwarf early-type galaxies with $R_{\rm e,gal}\approx1$~kpc) follow a shallow relation ($M_{\rm bh}\proptoσ_0^{2.5\text{--}3.1}$). Explained via the virial theorem, this flattening reframes expectations for intermediate-mass black holes. In contrast, tracing the `Disc Down-sizing' sequence - where dry mergers erase discs - yields a steep relation for massive elliptical and ellicular galaxies ($M_{\rm bh}\proptoσ_0^{7.8\pm1.4}$). The historical practice of applying a single, monolithic scaling relation across all morphological types averages over different formation histories, potentially skewing AGN virial $f$-factor calibrations and systematically under-predicting the ultra-massive black holes needed to generate the nanohertz gravitational wave background. Furthermore, strongly barred, dust-poor S0 galaxies appear offset to higher $σ_0$, while this dynamical signature is lost in the complexities of spiral galaxies. Ultimately, these morphology-dependent relations provide physically-motivated benchmarks for cosmological simulations and a framework for disentangling regimes driven by AGN feedback from those driven by collisionless mergers.

AI.tldr: This paper revisits the $M_{\rm bh}$–$σ_0$ relation using 137 galaxies with quantitative bar strengths and morphological awareness. Two distinct assembly pathways emerge: a shallow relation ($M_{\rm bh}\proptoσ_0^{2.5-3.1}$) for gas-poor S0/dwarf galaxies, and a steep relation ($M_{\rm bh}\proptoσ_0^{7.8±1.4}$) for massive ellipticals along the "Disc Down-sizing" sequence. The authors introduce SCOPE, a Bayesian hierarchical regression code that derives intrinsic population covariance with asymmetric error handling. Applying a single monolithic scaling relation across all types obscures formation histories, biases AGN virial calibrations, and underpredicts ultra-massive black holes needed for nanohertz gravitational wave background.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate that the $M_{\rm bh}$–$σ_0$ relation is not monolithic but bifurcates based on galaxy assembly pathways (gas-rich vs. gas-poor), and to provide physically-motivated, morphology-dependent benchmarks that improve black hole mass predictions, AGN virial factor calibrations, and cosmological simulations.
AI.method: A sample of 137 galaxies with quantitative bar strengths and enhanced morphological classification is analyzed within the 'Triangal' evolutionary framework. A symmetric Bayesian hierarchical regression code, SCOPE (Symmetric COvariance Population Estimator), is developed to derive the intrinsic population covariance while accommodating asymmetric measurement errors and ensuring directional invariance between axes.
AI.result: Two distinct scaling relations are found: (1) shallow slope for gas-poor S0/dwarf early-types ($M_{\rm bh}\proptoσ_0^{2.5-3.1}$), consistent with virial theorem expectations; (2) steep slope for massive ellipticals/ellicular galaxies ($M_{\rm bh}\proptoσ_0^{7.8±1.4}$), tracing the dry-merger-driven 'Disc Down-sizing' sequence. Strongly barred, dust-poor S0 galaxies show offsets to higher $σ_0$.
AI.conclusion: Monolithic scaling relations average over different formation histories, biasing AGN virial $f$-factor calibrations and underpredicting ultra-massive black holes relevant to the nanohertz gravitational wave background. Morphology-dependent relations provide physically-motivated benchmarks for simulations and help disentangle AGN feedback regimes from collisionless merger-driven regimes.

title: Phenomenology of Inflaton-Driven Early QCD Confinement and Solution to Axion Isocurvature Problem
comment: 48 pages, 10 figures
summary: We study the phenomenology of early QCD confinement during inflation, driven by a direct coupling between the inflaton and Standard Model gluons. This coupling dynamically raises the QCD confinement scale, making the axion sufficiently heavy to suppress isocurvature perturbations during the CMB epoch. As inflation proceeds, the confinement scale decreases and the axion becomes light, allowing de Sitter fluctuations during the late stages of inflation or post-inflationary thermal fluctuations to generate the observed dark matter abundance. In addition, QCD-induced corrections to the inflationary potential can shift the scalar spectral index towards smaller values, providing a further observational handle. We embed this mechanism in an $α$-attractor model of inflation and explore the resulting parameter space. We show that, in the minimal scenario with reheating into gluons, successful dark matter production requires deconfinement to occur shortly after the CMB window. Extensions involving reheating through heavy right-handed neutrinos generally require large Yukawa couplings, which induce sizable loop corrections that spoil inflationary dynamics. We show that this tension can be resolved in the presence of supersymmetry and derive constraints on the SUSY breaking scale that allow the mechanism to remain viable within plateau models of inflation. Treating the reheat temperature as a free parameter further enlarges the viable parameter space.

AI.tldr: The paper studies early QCD confinement during inflation via inflaton-gluon coupling, which raises the axion mass to suppress isocurvature perturbations. The axion later becomes light, generating dark matter from de Sitter or thermal fluctuations. The mechanism is embedded in α-attractor inflation models; minimal reheating into gluons requires deconfinement after the CMB window, while SUSY can resolve issues with neutrino-mediated reheating.
AI.motivation: To address the production of dark matter from axions while suppressing isocurvature perturbations during the CMB epoch, by dynamically varying the QCD confinement scale through inflaton-gluon coupling during inflation.
AI.method: The authors couple the inflaton to Standard Model gluons to dynamically raise/lower the QCD confinement scale, embed the mechanism in α-attractor inflation models, analyze parameter space for dark matter production via de Sitter or thermal fluctuations, and examine extensions with right-handed neutrino reheating and supersymmetry.
AI.result: In the minimal scenario (reheating into gluons), deconfinement must occur shortly after the CMB window. Neutrino-mediated reheating requires large Yukawa couplings that spoil inflation; SUSY resolves this with constraints on the SUSY breaking scale. Treating reheat temperature as a free parameter enlarges viable parameter space.
AI.conclusion: Early QCD confinement driven by inflaton-gluon coupling is a viable mechanism for axion dark matter production with suppressed isocurvature, provided specific timing of deconfinement and, in extended scenarios, appropriate SUSY breaking scales.

title: Early Results from GLASS-JWST. XXVI. Spatially Resolved Star Formation and Balmer Decrements at $1.1<z<2.3$ from NIRISS Slitless Spectroscopy
comment: 12 pages, 5 figures. Accepted for publication in ApJL
summary: Using JWST/NIRISS slitless spectroscopy, we present spatially resolved Balmer decrement measurements for 79 galaxies at $1.1 < z < 2.3$, which are gravitationally lensed by the foreground cluster Abell 2744. By stacking $\mathrm{H}α$ and $\mathrm{H}β$ emission maps in bins of stellar mass and redshift, we derive radial profiles of nebular dust attenuation and dust-corrected star formation rate (SFR). We find tentative evidence that the radial gradients of dust attenuation toward $\mathrm{H}α$ ($\rm A(\mathrm{H}α)$) vary with both redshift and stellar mass. At lower redshifts ($z = 1.10$--$1.53$), low-mass galaxies ($\rm 7.0<log(M_*/M_\odot)\leq8.5$) exhibit steeper $\rm A(Hα)$ gradients than higher-mass galaxies ($\rm 9.5<log(M_*/M_\odot)\leq11.0$), while the latter maintain detectable dust attenuation out to larger galactocentric radii. Galaxies at higher redshifts ($z = 1.76$--$2.29$) show lower attenuation levels. At fixed galactocentric radius, galaxies in the low-redshift bin generally exhibit higher dust attenuation than those at high redshifts, consistent with an increase in dust content toward later cosmic times. Dust-corrected SFR profiles in massive systems at lower redshifts are more spatially extended than those at higher redshifts, consistent with inside-out disk growth at $z\lesssim1.5$. These results suggest possible differences in attenuation properties across stellar mass and redshift bins, and demonstrate the power of gravitational lensing to probe internal structures in faint galaxies at sub-kiloparsec resolution.

AI.tldr: Using JWST/NIRISS slitless spectroscopy of 79 gravitationally lensed galaxies at $1.1<z<2.3$, we derive radial profiles of nebular dust attenuation ($\rm A(Hα)$) and dust-corrected SFR. We find that attenuation gradients vary with stellar mass and redshift, with lower-redshift, lower-mass galaxies showing steeper gradients, and massive systems exhibiting more extended SFR profiles at lower redshifts, consistent with inside-out disk growth.
AI.motivation: To understand how nebular dust attenuation and star formation rate profiles vary with stellar mass and redshift at cosmic noon, leveraging gravitational lensing to achieve sub-kiloparsec resolution in faint galaxies.
AI.method: JWST/NIRISS slitless spectroscopy of 79 gravitationally lensed galaxies at $1.1<z<2.3$ behind Abell 2744; spatially resolved Balmer decrement measurements; stacking Hα and Hβ emission maps in bins of stellar mass and redshift to derive radial profiles.
AI.result: Radial gradients of $\rm A(Hα)$ vary with redshift and stellar mass: lower-redshift ($z=1.10$–$1.53$), low-mass galaxies have steeper gradients; higher-redshift ($z=1.76$–$2.29$) galaxies show lower attenuation; dust-corrected SFR profiles are more extended in massive systems at lower redshifts.
AI.conclusion: Results suggest differences in attenuation properties across mass and redshift, with inside-out disk growth at $z\lesssim1.5$, demonstrating gravitational lensing's power for sub-kpc internal structure studies of faint galaxies.

title: What it takes to solve the Hubble tension through Modifications of Cosmological Recombination II: in light of ACT DR6 and DESI DR2
comment: 7+3 pages, 5 figures. Comments are welcome
summary: We construct data-driven solutions to the Hubble tension, in light of recent data from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT DR6) and the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI DR2). We search for the minimal modification to the recombination history through a time-varying electron mass $m_e(z)$ that increases the best-fit $H_0$ inferred from CMB data toward the SH0ES value, without worsening the fit to the data. Using Planck and ACT data including lensing, we find a perturbative modification to $m_e(z)$ that fully resolves the Hubble tension, with the solution sharing the same qualitative oscillatory structure as in previous work using Planck data alone, demonstrating its robustness to the inclusion of more precise and independent CMB data. As a byproduct, the solution also eases the $S_8$ tension. Once DESI DR2 BAO data are added, however, perturbative modifications to $m_e(z)$ cannot fully resolve the Hubble tension. This reflects the same fundamental limitation: raising $H_0$ by modifying recombination generically lowers $Ω_m$, being inconsistent with late-time cosmological observations.

AI.tldr: The paper explores whether time-varying electron mass during recombination can resolve the Hubble tension using Planck, ACT DR6, and DESI DR2 data. While CMB-only data allow a solution (with oscillatory structure robust across experiments), adding DESI BAO data prevents full resolution because modifying recombination to raise H₀ lowers Ωₘ, conflicting with late-time observations.
AI.motivation: To construct data-driven solutions to the Hubble tension by searching for minimal modifications to recombination history (via a time-varying electron mass mₑ(z)) that increase H₀ toward the SH0ES value, using the latest CMB and BAO data.
AI.method: Perturbative modification to the electron mass as a function of redshift mₑ(z) is introduced. The analysis uses Planck, ACT DR6 (including lensing), and DESI DR2 BAO data to search for modifications that improve the fit to CMB data while raising H₀.
AI.result: With Planck + ACT data alone, a perturbative mₑ(z) modification fully resolves the Hubble tension, with an oscillatory structure robust across datasets, and also eases the S₈ tension. However, adding DESI DR2 BAO data prevents full resolution because raising H₀ via recombination modifications lowers Ωₘ, inconsistent with late-time observations.
AI.conclusion: Perturbative modifications to recombination cannot fully resolve the Hubble tension when late-time BAO data from DESI DR2 are included, due to a fundamental limitation: increasing H₀ by modifying recombination reduces Ωₘ, conflicting with late-time cosmological constraints.

title: Near- to Far-Infrared Spectral Energy Distribution Analysis of Interacting Galaxies in Hickson Compact Groups 56 and Stephan's Quintet (HCG 92)
comment: This is a pre-copyedited, author-produced version of an article accepted for publication in "Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan'' following peer review
summary: We investigate star formation activity in galaxies belonging to two Hickson Compact Groups (HCGs), HCG 56 and HCG 92 (Stephan's Quintet), both of which show clear evidence of interactions, using spectral energy distribution (SED) analysis across the near- to far-infrared range. By combining data from the Infrared Satellite AKARI, the Spitzer Space Telescope, and the Herschel Space Observatory, we examine how galactic interactions influence the physical conditions and the evolution of group members. The observed SEDs of member galaxies are compared with model SEDs representing both star-forming galaxies and active galactic nuclei (AGN). Star formation rates (SFRs) are estimated using two independent methods: (i) the strength of mid-infrared polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) bands and (ii) far-infrared luminosities attributed to star formation, as derived from the models. Although both methods yield generally consistent results, SFRs based on PAH features are systematically lower, possibly due to the PAH destruction in some interacting galaxies. When plotted against the stellar mass, all member galaxies are found below the main sequence of star-forming galaxies in the SDSS field, suggesting that interaction-induced starbursts are not seen in HCG 56 and HCG 92.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes star formation in two interacting Hickson Compact Groups (HCG 56 and HCG 92/Stephan's Quintet) using infrared SED analysis from AKARI, Spitzer, and Herschel. SFRs estimated from PAH bands and far-infrared luminosities are generally consistent, though PAH-based SFRs are systematically lower, possibly due to PAH destruction. All member galaxies lie below the main sequence of star-forming galaxies, indicating no interaction-induced starbursts.
AI.motivation: To investigate how galactic interactions in compact groups influence star formation activity and the physical conditions/evolution of group members.
AI.method: SED analysis across near- to far-infrared using AKARI, Spitzer, and Herschel data. SFRs estimated via two methods: (i) PAH band strengths and (ii) far-infrared luminosities from model fits. Model SEDs for star-forming galaxies and AGN were compared with observed SEDs.
AI.result: SFRs from both methods are broadly consistent, but PAH-based SFRs are systematically lower. All member galaxies lie below the main sequence of star-forming galaxies when plotted against stellar mass.
AI.conclusion: Interaction-induced starbursts are not occurring in HCG 56 and HCG 92; PAH destruction may affect SFR estimates in interacting environments.

title: The quenching time and timescale distribution of z~2 quiescent galaxies from precise colour distribution analysis
comment: Submitted to OJA, comments welcome. Code will be made available on acceptance
